accounting.rationale: PDF 78, printed 64, line 14 introduces the TYPE specifier's three categories; R703 owns the syntax. This sentence supplies no independent execution or diagnostic oracle.
TYPE(*) is the assumed-type route defined in p3 and restricted by C714-C716; it is not a declaration of a concrete type.
The intrinsic alternative includes all five intrinsic types and their separately governed parameters, not just INTEGER.
Nonintrinsic includes derived, enum and enumeration types. An unnamed interoperable enumeration's integer enumerators do not stand in for a named enum type.
PDF 78 lines 15-20 contains a real declaration-order restriction, three function-prefix availability routes, and a result-declaration interpretation.
The function-prefix exception is conditional on the function result and a definition within that function body; it does not allow arbitrary forward object declarations.
PDF 78 lines 21-24 separates assumed/unlimited terminology and absence of a declared type from the dynamic-type and parameter propagation effect.
TYPE(*) declares an assumed-type entity. TYPEOF is neither used nor treated as equivalent.
An assumed-type entity is unlimited polymorphic, but the TYPE(*) use restrictions still apply. This does not authorize the SELECT TYPE uses available to CLASS(*).
No declared type is assigned by TYPE(*); an effective argument's current type does not become the dummy's declared type.
There is no same-declared-type relation to any entity, including a second unlimited polymorphic entity. This is distinct from directional type compatibility in 7.3.3 and dynamic-type equality.
PDF 78 lines 25-26; all eight restrictions are separated, including dummy data object rather than merely dummy.
PDF 78 lines 27-30; both prohibited contexts, the assumed-type receiver exception, first-argument qualification and all eight named inquiry/address exceptions are retained.
PDF 78 lines 31-32; both the assumed-type actual and assumed-rank receiver premises are necessary.

requirements.title: Assumed-type entities are eligible dummy data objects
requirements.definition: An assumed-type entity must be a dummy data object, not an ordinary local or a dummy procedure. It cannot have ALLOCATABLE, CODIMENSION, INTENT(OUT), POINTER or VALUE and cannot be an explicit-shape array. Scalar, assumed-shape, assumed-size and assumed-rank dummy data objects are not excluded by this constraint. Other attributes and uses remain subject to their own rules.
requirements.oracle: Eight compile-only invalid/control pairs change only the offending dummy-list entry, EXTERNAL or prohibited attribute, or explicit upper bound. The codimension case is a scalar nonallocatable dummy with legal explicit coshape and requests coarray mode. Four independent runtime admission controls use allowed scalar and array forms and return checked inquiry sentinels without reading assumed-type payloads.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The repairs deliberately remain compile-only controls, not claimed runtime effects. No caller introduces an allocatable/pointer/rank mismatch into an invalid declaration. The six attribute/shape negatives declare lines 1-3 as a single-entity specification span: the SUBROUTINE dummy binding and its explicit attribute/shape declaration are both endpoints of that entity's restriction. The END statement at line 4 is excluded, so a whole-procedure recovery range does not fit. Nondummy and procedure negatives retain exact declaration points. Every accepted report also needs a causal eligibility/attribute/shape message; same-line unsupported-feature text cannot substitute. Paired control and source-message review remain necessary even when the automated gate matches. Coarray implementation failures are failures, not optional-profile skips. Reporting capability under 4.2 is not mandatory fatal rejection.
requirements.dependencies: 4.1.2 p3 and 4.2 p2(3), PDF 45-46; 8.2/R801 (PDF 117), 8.5.6/C826/C828 (PDF 121-122), 8.5.8.2-.7 (PDF 125-129), and 15.4.2.2 (PDF 325). C715 separately limits every use of the admitted dummy.

requirements.title: Assumed-type names have a bounded set of permitted uses
requirements.definition: An assumed-type variable name cannot occur in a designator or expression except as an actual argument for an assumed-type dummy, or as the first argument of IS_CONTIGUOUS, LBOUND, PRESENT, RANK, SHAPE, SIZE, UBOUND or ISO_C_BINDING's C_LOC. Being unlimited polymorphic does not add CLASS(*) operations to TYPE(*). The exceptions do not waive the named procedure's argument, state, rank, OPTIONAL, TARGET, contiguity or size requirements.

pending.later-argument-source-use: Needs a finite canonical source-use join for the later argument positions of all eight permitted procedures. Replacing DIM or KIND with an assumed-type dummy also violates independent integer/scalar/constant-expression premises, so it is not a clean C715-only negative. The first-position controls and STORAGE_SIZE-to-RANK repair do not prove exclusion in every later position. No evidence-link schema is invented in this batch.

requirements.oracle: Six independently compiled controls exercise forwarding, contiguity, bounds/shape/size, optional presence, rank and C_LOC. Three compile-report pairs isolate an assumed-type array-element designator passed to a scalar TYPE(*) receiver, an unlisted STORAGE_SIZE inquiry, and forwarding to CLASS(*) rather than TYPE(*). Repairs change the designator's source declaration to INTEGER, the inquiry to RANK, or the receiver keyword to TYPE. Each diagnostic is located on the single offending statement and must describe the prohibited assumed-type use.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The designator pair has a scalar receiver, so neither C716 nor an array-rank mismatch is introduced. STORAGE_SIZE admits a data object of any type; KIND would add an independent intrinsic-type premise. CLASS(*) is type compatible with all entities, so its forbidden receipt of TYPE(*) is not a concrete-type mismatch. PRESENT is applied only to an OPTIONAL dummy; no other inquiry uses an absent argument. Bounds and sizes use initialized nonzero arrays, and the contiguity control specifies CONTIGUOUS rather than demanding a processor-dependent section layout. C_LOC uses a live scalar TARGET of C_INT kind and compares C pointers with C_ASSOCIATED, never as integers. Generic type mismatch, recovery ranges and unsupported syntax are not substitute evidence.
requirements.dependencies: 4.2 p2(3), PDF 46; C714/C716 and 7.3.3; 8.5.7 (PDF 123-124); 15.5.2.4-.5 (PDF 339-340); 16.9.115/119/163/171/185/194/200/215 (PDF 424-425,445,449,456,459,462,469); 18.2.3.2 and 18.2.3.7 (PDF 518,523). Canonical intrinsic semantics and C ABI coverage are dependencies, not newly owned requirements.

requirements.title: Assumed-type forwarding to assumed-rank preserves descriptor eligibility
requirements.definition: When an assumed-type actual corresponds to an assumed-rank dummy, the actual must itself be assumed-shape or assumed-rank. An ordinary scalar assumed-type dummy and an assumed-size assumed-type dummy do not meet this condition. An assumed-rank actual may have scalar effective rank; a concrete-type scalar actual is outside the assumed-type premise.
requirements.oracle: Two compile-report pairs forward scalar or assumed-size TYPE(*) to an explicitly interfaced TYPE(*) assumed-rank receiver. Repairs change only the forwarding dummy's shape form to assumed-rank or assumed-shape. Three runtime controls check assumed-shape forwarding, assumed-rank forwarding with scalar and array effective arguments, and a concrete INTEGER scalar outside the premise.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The invalid assumed-size form is legal under C714; an explicit-shape TYPE(*) negative would not isolate C716. The receiving assumed-rank accepts either actual rank, so the repaired shape change does not cure a second ordinary rank mismatch. All calls are to assumed-type receivers, satisfying C715. Exact call-point and causal reporting gates apply; a whole-procedure recovery range cannot satisfy the point. Runtime sentinels start negative and do not inspect unknown payloads.

requirements.title: TYPE declarations require an available previously defined named type
requirements.definition: In a type declaration statement, a derived, enum or enumeration specifier within TYPE must name a previously defined type. For a function result, specifying the type in the FUNCTION statement is also permitted when the definition is inside the function or the type is available there through use or host association. The function exception does not permit arbitrary forward declarations of other objects.

pending.ordering-source-use: Needs a canonical declaration-order/use graph with independently reviewed exclusion evidence: derived type definition/access premises, enum C7112 and enumeration C7116, and any applicable Clause 19 reporting route. The allowed declarations here are positive controls, not proof that every forbidden forward reference is reported. The prose's shall alone does not supply a mandatory S diagnostic, and no new LFortran rejection policy is imposed.

requirements.oracle: Four runtime positive controls use a prior derived type and host-associated function prefix, a USE-only prefix whose caller imports the type under a different name, a previously defined named enum, and a previously defined enumeration type. Small returned/component/ordinal values are checked.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The two F2023 nonderived controls retain their actual value oracles if a compiler lacks the syntax. They are not replaced by integer or unnamed-ENUM controls. Function-result interpretation for body-local definitions is separately exercised by S7.3.2.2-002. Coverage is not automatically credited to defining 7.5/7.6 constraints.
requirements.dependencies: 7.1.2, 7.3.2.1/R703, 7.5.2.4 (PDF 90), 7.6.1/C7112 and 7.6.2/C7116 (PDF 109-112), 8.2 (PDF 117), 15.6.2.2 p3-p4 (PDF 354), and the canonical USE/host-association rules in 19.5.1. 4.1.2 p3 distinguishes prose restrictions from numbered reporting obligations.

requirements.title: A function-prefix TYPE result follows its body-local type definition
requirements.definition: When a function result's TYPE specifier is in the FUNCTION statement and names a type defined in that function body, the result is interpreted as declared with that type immediately after the definition. The result's other attributes still need their ordinary specification; the type and parameters must not be redundantly specified both in the prefix and a result declaration.
requirements.oracle: Three independent functions define their result type inside the body and return initialized values. The nonpolymorphic derived result is expanded by formatted internal I/O to its single public INTEGER component; SS,I0 plus checked IOSTAT and an initialized record gives an exact decimal result. Named enum and enumeration results are converted by INT and compared to their expected integer/ordinal values.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The body-defined types are not silently moved into a host module to satisfy a compiler. No local type has private, pointer, allocatable or type-bound components. The controls do not assert processor storage layout or read an uninitialized result. Unsupported F2023 results retain runtime expectations.
requirements.dependencies: 15.6.2.2 p3-p4 (PDF 354); 7.6.1-.2 (PDF 109-112); 12.6.3 p4-p8 and 12.6.4.1 (PDF 263-264); 13.7.2.1-.2 (PDF 295-296); 16.9.110 p3/p5(iv)-(v), INT (PDF 421-422). Runtime interpretation, not blanket error reporting, follows 4.2 p2(1).

requirements.title: Assumed-type dynamic type and parameters come from the effective argument
requirements.definition: An assumed-type entity takes its dynamic type and type parameter values from its effective argument. It still has no declared type. Effective argument is the argument-associated entity, not necessarily the spelling of the ultimate actual. The separate restrictions on derived actuals with parameters, type-bound procedures or final subroutines continue to apply.

pending.assumed-derived-identity-source-use: Needs a canonical source-use witness for the identity of permitted nonparameterized derived effective arguments, retaining 15.5.2.5 p2's exclusions. CFI_type_struct/CFI_type_other, addresses and storage sizes cannot distinguish arbitrary named derived types. C715 forbids directly substituting SELECT TYPE, SAME_TYPE_AS or EXTENDS_TYPE_OF on TYPE(*). A finite source/association join is pending; this is not a claim that every possible indirect oracle is impossible.

requirements.oracle: A real mixed-language runtime fixture forwards an assumed-rank TYPE(*) dummy to an assumed-type BIND(C) receiver. The initialized actuals use the mandatory C_INT kind, supported default/double REAL kind inquiries and default CHARACTER at two lengths. The checker validates scalar rank, nonnull base address, CFI_VERSION, a type code mapped to the actual Fortran category/kind, and elem_len. Fortran derives an eligibility flag for every integer or real macro counterpart in Table 18.4 by comparing supported ISO_C_BINDING kind values. Distinct C type codes for the same Fortran kind are accepted only through that source-supported mapping, not merely because storage sizes match. Default CHARACTER must map to C_CHAR; its two expected lengths are 3 and 5 bytes. All status sentinels are initialized. No dimension or payload is dereferenced and no private descriptor layout is reproduced.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The selected Fortran processor's matching ISO_Fortran_binding.h and ABI-compatible companion C configuration are required. The C build step explicitly requests that processor header; only its bytes are staged, with path/hash and companion identity recorded and snapshot-checked. A separate standard-property profile qualifies the optional default/double-real and default-character C mappings before the fixture executes; failure of mandatory C_INT is an error, not an optional skip. Optional negative C kind constants are never used as declaration kinds. The in-fixture mapping guard remains an explicit consistency check, not a fallback to another kind or an empty control. C codes are not assumed unique for a Fortran kind: category-separated alias flags preserve the Table 18.4 relation rather than inferring identity from sizeof. Header/version mismatch is an interface failure before local type/parameter propagation is observed. A successful run still needs independent interface qualification; no arbitrary derived-type identity or general compatibility is inferred.
requirements.dependencies: C714-C716; 15.5.2.4 p6 and 15.5.2.5 p2 (PDF 339-340); 18.2.2 p2-p6, including negative unsupported-kind constants (PDF 516-517); 18.3.7 p2(5) (PDF 529), 18.4/18.5.1 (PDF 531), 18.5.2-.4, Table 18.4 and NOTE 2 (PDF 531-535). No owned coverage is claimed for those canonical interoperability requirements.

review_rationale: Independent source/link review and verified integration: doc/source_audits/batch_008.json. C714-C716 and assumed-type premises preserve dummy data, attribute/shape, allowed-use and forwarding conditions. Diagnostic exclusions now reject causal-looking implementation-gap messages. The descriptor effect has an independently qualified mapping/header interface; arbitrary derived-type identity remains outside its observable scope.
